overview.subtitle: Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar. It is a month of fasting from dawn to sunset, focused worship, Quran recitation, community care, and spiritual renewal.
body: The Quran describes Ramadan as the month in which the Quran was revealed as guidance for humanity. Muslims fast to develop taqwa (God-consciousness), discipline their desires, and increase empathy for those in need.
Beyond fasting, Ramadan is a time to elevate worship through prayer, charity, and reflection. Families gather, communities host iftars, and masajid become centers of learning and service.
Every day in Ramadan is an invitation to reset habits, strengthen spiritual focus, and renew intentions with sincerity.
key_points: Fasting is an act of worship and self-discipline.
Ramadan is the month in which the Quran was revealed.
The last ten nights are especially blessed, including Laylat al-Qadr.
Charity and community care are central to the month.
Every day is an opportunity to improve character and habits.

history.subtitle: Ramadan is tied to the first revelation of the Quran and remains central to Islamic worship. The practice of fasting in Ramadan began with the early Muslim community and continues globally today.
body: The Quran establishes fasting as a prescribed act for believers, linking Ramadan directly to revelation and guidance. Over centuries, communities have preserved the rhythm of fasting, nightly prayers, and charity as a shared spiritual culture.
The month is also a time of moral renewal - improving character, speech, and relationships. This spiritual focus is one reason Ramadan remains the most cherished month in the Islamic calendar.
Across the world, Ramadan brings together families, neighbors, and communities to build stronger bonds and shared purpose.

how_to_fast.intro: Fasting is from dawn to sunset with the intention (niyyah). The goal is worship, discipline, and avoiding what breaks the fast.

cards.title: Do's
items: Eat a balanced Suhoor and hydrate well.
Pray on time and read Quran daily.
Break fast promptly at sunset with dates and water if possible.
Be mindful of behavior, speech, and time.
Make dua before Iftar - it is a special time for acceptance.

cards.title: Don'ts
items: Do not eat or drink between Fajr and Maghrib.
Avoid backbiting, arguments, and harmful speech.
Do not neglect prayers or Quran.
Avoid wasting time in unhelpful activities.

prayers_made_easy.intro: Keep prayers simple and consistent. Focus on quality, not perfection.
daily_prayer_tips: Pray on time even if the prayer is short.
Keep a small list of duas you repeat daily.
Use prayer as your daily reset points.
If you miss a prayer, make it up as soon as you can.

taraweeh.title: Taraweeh (Night Prayer)
taraweeh.description: Taraweeh is a special night prayer in Ramadan. Pray in congregation or at home. Even a small portion is valuable.
tips: Start with a shorter number of rakaat and build consistency.
Follow the local masjid schedule or pray at home with family.
Keep a gentle pace and focus on reflection.
If you miss a night, return the next - consistency matters most.
checklist: Read from the Quran if possible.
End with a short dua for acceptance.

charity_guide.intro: Charity is central in Ramadan. Zakat al-Fitr is obligatory before Eid prayer, while ongoing sadaqah builds compassion.
overview: Zakat al-Fitr purifies the fasting person from minor shortcomings and ensures everyone can celebrate Eid with dignity.
Sadaqah is voluntary charity given throughout the month. Even small, consistent giving can have a large impact.

zakat_al_fitr.title: Zakat al-Fitr basics
points: A required charity per person in the household, given before Eid prayer.
Paid before Eid prayer, preferably during Ramadan.
